Exit routes blocked or poorly maintained
Egress
Walk the entire escape route. Note stored items, damage, or other obstructions, with exact locations and photos; check the applicable maintenance provisions.
Exit doors or escape components difficult to use
Exit doors
Check door operation, locking hardware, stairs, ramps, and other escape components present. Record the specific concern and verify the applicable component subsection and exceptions.
Exit capacity does not match the use
Occupancy
Compare documented occupant load with available escape capacity. Record actual use, measurements, and supporting plans before deciding whether a deficiency exists.
Too few usable exits
Egress
Count usable escape options for the actual occupancy. Check the governing occupancy chapter and permitted exceptions before identifying a missing exit.
Exit arrangement leaves inadequate alternatives
Egress
Sketch the available escape paths and identify points where routes converge. Compare the arrangement with the requirements applicable to this occupancy.
Travel route to an exit is too long
Egress
Measure the actual travel path around obstructions. Record the route, occupancy, and protection features; verify the applicable distance limit before citing.
Exit discharge is obstructed or unsafe
Egress
Follow exits to their discharge destinations. Document storage, locked gates, or unsafe conditions and compare the route with the applicable discharge provisions.
Normal lighting along escape routes is inadequate
Lighting and signs
Observe lighting throughout the escape route under its normal operating conditions. Record dark locations and any measurements needed for code review.
Emergency lighting does not operate or lacks test evidence
Lighting and signs
Review required emergency lighting, its condition, and available test documentation. Arrange testing through the responsible person; record failures and missing evidence.
Exit identification is missing, obscured, or misleading
Lighting and signs
Review signs and route identification from an occupant's viewpoint. Record missing, hidden, damaged, or confusing markings and verify what this occupancy requires.
Fire-resistance separation is damaged or breached
Fire and smoke separation
Record damaged rated assemblies, suspect penetrations, and opening-protection concerns. Compare observed conditions with approved assemblies and the applicable barrier provisions.
Smoke partition integrity is compromised
Fire and smoke separation
Where smoke partitions are required, inspect visible continuity and protected openings. Document damage and unprotected openings for comparison with the approved design.
Smoke barrier integrity is compromised
Fire and smoke separation
Identify required smoke barriers and document visible gaps, penetrations, or opening-protection concerns. Verify the relevant barrier requirements and approved construction.
Vertical opening protection is incomplete
Fire and smoke separation
Identify unprotected openings between levels, including shafts and floor openings. Verify the applicable protection method and exceptions before recording a deficiency.
Hazardous rooms or activities lack required protection
Hazardous areas
Record the actual hazardous use, materials, and existing protection. Compare separation or suppression measures with the applicable special-hazard provisions and occupancy chapter.
Door inspection or testing records are missing
Fire doors
Identify door assemblies subject to inspection or testing. Review documentation and unresolved defects; verify the applicable door type and referenced standard.
Utility installations present a life-safety concern
Building systems
Record visible electrical, gas, or other utility concerns and their locations. Refer to the applicable utility subsection and referenced installation standard for the exact requirement.
Heating, ventilation, or cooking equipment needs review
Building systems
Identify the equipment and observed condition. Review the applicable heating, ventilation, or cooking provisions and referenced standards before specifying corrective work.
Alarm or detection system has unresolved problems
Alarms
Record panel indications, damaged devices, and available service or test records. Verify system requirements for the occupancy and document unresolved deficiencies.
Sprinkler protection appears impaired or incomplete
Water systems

Record visible sprinkler-system concerns and compare coverage with the actual use and approved design. Review applicable requirements and referenced standards with the responsible system professional.
Extinguishers are missing, inaccessible, or unserviceable
Extinguishers
Where extinguishers are required, review placement, access, condition, and maintenance evidence. Use the referenced extinguisher standard for the detailed requirement.
Standpipe equipment or required protection needs correction
Water systems
Document visible standpipe concerns and verify the required system for the building. Consult the referenced installation standard and approved system information.
Fire-protection maintenance or impairment records are incomplete
Water systems
Review system testing, maintenance, impairment handling, and retained documentation. Identify unresolved defects and missing records under the applicable operating provisions.
Interior finish lacks evidence of suitability
Interior finish and contents
Identify changed wall, ceiling, or floor finishes. Request supporting classifications and compare their proposed use with the applicable occupancy requirements.
Decorations or vegetation need fire-safety review
Interior finish and contents
Record decorative materials, curtains, or vegetation and their locations. Verify applicable restrictions and supporting treatment or performance documentation before requiring correction.
